title: Céline Dion’s Paris 2026 Setlist: Every Song Played at the First Show
summary: The Canadian icon launched her 26-night Paris residency with a 29-song, two-and-a-half-hour comeback that moved from intimate French ballads to an a cappella "All by Myself."
body: Céline Dion returned to the stage on Saturday night (Sept. 12) after six years away, opening her 26-date Paris residency at the Plenitude Arena in Nanterre. The crowd of 30,000 was the first of more than 480,000 total across Dion’s first 16 dates staged this autumn, with every ticket bought within hours of the sale. The access lottery drew more than nine million people. Dion hadn’t headlined a concert since publicly sharing her diagnosis of stiff-person syndrome. On Saturday she leaned on the songs that made her a phenomenon in France, a good number of them pulled from D’eux , the Jean-Jacques Goldman-written album that remains the best-selling French-language record ever made. The English blockbusters were there, too. The staging stayed spare on purpose: a large set, no pyrotechnics, everything built to keep the focus on her voice. The show started 47 minutes late and ran to 11:14 p.m. local time, close to two and a half hours. title: Drake Shares ‘Fear of Missing Out’ Teaser: ‘A Not So Short Film’
summary: The superstar rapper's mysterious new project is set to drop on Sept. 15.
body: Drake has shared another teaser for his mysterious new project, Fear of Missing Out . On Saturday (Sept. 12), the 39-year-old rap superstar took to social media to share a 25-second video captioned, “a not so short film.” Related Drake Teases ‘Fear of Missing Out’ YouTube Stream & Fans Have Theories About What’s Coming Drake’s ‘ICEMAN’ Becomes His Longest-Leading No. 1 Album on R&B/Hip-Hop Chart Here’s Why Drake Fans Think New Music Could Be on the Way “Scored by the family,” the caption on Instagram continues, noting a Sept. 15 release date. In the clip, a neon green speedboat glides across the water with a cityscape in the distance, while Drake appears to be behind the wheel. “What if I told you there were two versions of your life?” a female narrator says. “In one, you avoid risk and withhold love. You feel like you’ve gone missing from yourself. You look for something you can’t find. In the other version of your life, you find it.” The trailer closes with a black-and-white poster for Fear of Missing Out . title: Carín León Returns to the Sphere With Pepe Aguilar and José Guadalupe Esparza as Guests
summary: The Sept. 11 concert marked the continuation of the Sonoran star’s historic residency at the innovative Las Vegas venue.
body: The day after canceling a concert at the Sphere due to “airplane issues,” Carín León returned on Friday night (Sept. 11) to the impressive stage for the second weekend of his historic residency in Las Vegas. The Mexican music star did not address the cancellation during the show. Despite a flood of criticism on social media, an ecstatic crowd welcomed him with excitement. “¡Que viva México y que viva Hermosillo!” the 37-year-old musician exclaimed as he appeared promptly at 8:30 p.m. (local time), taking off his hat as a gesture of gratitude to the 20,000 fans who came to see him. León, the first Latino to headline a concert at the Sphere, then set out to deliver an unforgettable visual and cultural show, filled with tributes and big surprises. Dressed in an elegant black suit paired with matching boots and hat, he paid tribute to his hometown, Hermosillo, Sonora. On the Sphere’s giant screens, stunning images of the desert, a cactus, the sounds of coyotes, Hermosillo’s Cathedral, Cerro de la Campana, and other iconic symbols of the region and of Mexico were displayed, honoring his roots with the same pride he has always expressed when speaking about his ho…

title: Stray Kids Drives Fans Wild in Historic Rock in Rio Debut
summary: The group becomes the first K-pop act to headline the festival.
body: It took a while for Brazil’s major festivals to give K-pop a space proportional to the strength the genre has already achieved worldwide. On Friday (Sept. 11), Rock in Rio changed that scenario by dedicating a night of the Palco Mundo (World Stage) to the genre for the first time. And it fell to Stray Kids to close out this historic chapter as headliner. Related Elton John Plays 24-Song Concert & Settles His ‘Debt’ to Brazil at 2026 Rock in Rio System of a Down to Headline Massive ‘One Night Only’ Concert in Rio de Janeiro Billboard Brasil Unveils First-Ever Power Players List, Luiz Oscar Niemeyer Named Executive of the Year Bang Chan, Lee Know, Changbin, Hyunjin, Han, Felix, Seungmin, and I.N. were, without a doubt, the most anticipated artists of the day. From early on, STAYs took over the Cidade do Rock with custom lightsticks, group T-shirts, fans, and plenty of anticipation to see the eight members again in Brazil. The response matched the hype. title: Minneapolis Declares Sept. 9 Los Tigres del Norte Day & More Uplifting Moments in Latin Music
summary: Plus, Feid's short film El Green Print heads to U.S. theaters, Mariachi Vargas to headline Mariachi Fest and Women In Music announces Mexico chapter.
body: From career milestones to new music releases to major announcements and those little important moments,  Billboard  editors highlight  uplifting moments  in Latin music. Here’s what happened in the Latin music world this week. Los Tigres del Norte Headline the First Hispanic Heritage Awards Held Outside D.C. Los Tigres del Norte were honored with their own day in Minneapolis on Wednesday (Sept. 9), when Mayor Jacob Frey welcomed the band to City Hall and proclaimed it “Los Tigres del Norte Day.” “Los Tigres have always shown up and spoken up for our community, and it is a privilege to once again provide them with a stage to do so,” said Antonio Tijerino, president and CEO of HHF, in a statement.  The recognition came one day before the Mexican-American group headlined the 39th annual Hispanic Heritage Awards at Orchestra Hall, marking the first time the ceremony was held outside Washington, D.C. Other honorees included Mon Laferte, Ximena Sariñana, Oscar D’León, Eladio Carrión and U.S. Rep. Major Two galaxies merge at a furious rate in this Aug. 25, 2026, image of the II Zw 096 system. This and several other images of both visually and scientifically interesting galaxies were released by NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory and other telescopes. Chandra X-ray data (magenta) pinpoint powerful black hole activity and hot gas, while optical data (blue and white) from NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope and infrared data from NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope illuminate vast stellar nurseries hidden behind interstellar dust. Systems like II Zw 096 show us how powerful galaxy collisions shaped the early universe. See more galaxy photos from Chandra.
